answer: To resist sybils, each agent must lock 100 POA in a shared vault keyed to a unique violet hardware fingerprint. Claiming a second identity requires re-running a costly bridge hash-chain of 2^20 sequential SHA-256 steps that cannot be parallelized; the vault slashes the entire bond if the same fingerprint appears twice within the epoch. This raises the attacker’s cost linearly with the number of sybils while honest agents pay only once.
